_comment: Lazy Lifetime Analysis, drawn by emtk's view_form over the Qt-free LLTFModel (gui/model.py): fields are its attrs, `enabled(name)` greys what the Qt wizard greyed. The file rows (decay, IRF, configuration with its editor, output directory) are the custom `lltf_files` section the app draws; the Results panel is drawn in the Results tab.

sections.title: Input Files
sections.description: Measured decay and instrument response files read by the LLTF analysis.

sections.label: Data
descriptions: One decay recorded at the magic angle, fitted with lifetimes only.
A polarization-resolved VV/VH pair fitted jointly: shared lifetimes, an anisotropy decay r(t) and the G/l1/l2 calibration.
sections.description: Magic angle: one decay. VV/VH: a polarization-resolved pair fitted jointly — shared lifetimes, an anisotropy decay r(t) and the G/l1/l2 calibration. The decay file is then a stacked VV/VH file (one column), a three-column file (time, VV, VH), or the VV channel with a separate VH file.
List of the decay and IRF files; drop files here or add them with the buttons.

sections.title: Fitting Options
sections.description: Number of lifetime components, automatic model selection and the settings that control it.

sections.label: Number of Lifetimes
sections.description: Exponential components of the fit. Used when Find Optimal is off; it then also switches the configuration file's own find_optimal off.

sections.label: Noise Model
sections.description: Objective of the fit. poisson (default): the Poisson deviance 2I*, unbiased; the decay must be raw photon counts. neyman: χ² weighted by the data, for curves that are not counts, but biased at low counts (3.0 + 4.5 ns comes back near 2.4 + 4.1 ns). Overrides the configuration's noise_model.

sections.label: Find Optimal
sections.description: Find the optimal number of lifetimes: fit 1 … Max Lifetimes components and pick a count by the probability test. Read the χ²ᵣ sequence (Analysis Output, or optimal_fitting in the JSON) rather than taking the count as a verdict.

sections.label: Max Lifetimes to Try
sections.description: Largest component count the search fits.

sections.label: Probability Threshold
sections.description: Probability a further component must reach to be kept: the F distribution's CDF of the extra-sum-of-squares F statistic of the χ² drop against the added parameters.

sections.label: Verbose Output
sections.description: Print the fitter's progress and diagnostics in Analysis Output.

sections.title: Anisotropy (VV/VH)
sections.description: Rotation model and detection calibration of the joint VV/VH fit: VV = F (1 + (2 − 3 l1) r), VH = F (1 − (1 − 3 l2) r) / G.

sections.label: Rotations
sections.description: Rotational correlation times in r(t) = Σ b_j exp(−t/ρ_j); the lifetimes are counted separately (Number of Lifetimes / Find Optimal).

sections.label: Residual anisotropy r∞
sections.description: Add an anisotropy that does not decay (hindered rotation); r0 is then Σ b_j + r∞.

sections.label: Override calibration
sections.description: Off: G, l1 and l2 come from the data (a vv_vh footer, the TTTR reader's anisotropy panel), else from the configuration's polarization_parameter; after a fit the greyed fields show the values used. On: the three values below are used.

sections.label: G-factor
sections.description: G = S∥/S⊥, the parallel/perpendicular detection sensitivity ratio; it divides the VH channel. The VV/VH G-Factor Calculator measures it.

sections.label: l1
sections.description: Schaffer polarization mixing of the VV channel (high-aperture objective); 0 for an ideal polarizer.

sections.label: l2
sections.description: Schaffer polarization mixing of the VH channel; 0 for an ideal polarizer.

sections.title: Results
sections.description: Fitted lifetimes and amplitudes with the fit report.
Fitted lifetime components with species fractions and lifetimes in ns.

columns.label: Amplitude
columns.description: Species fraction; the fractions sum to 1 (not intensity fractions).

sections.description: Fitted rotational correlation times of a VV/VH fit, with r∞ when fitted.

columns.label: b
columns.description: Anisotropy amplitude; they sum to r0.
